page: Microsoft Azure M32ms is a memory-optimized server instance belonging to the MS family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8280M processor with an x86_64 architecture, featuring 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 2.7 GHz. The processor includes a 105 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 875.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 27.34 GB per core. It also features 1049 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile characterized by average multi-core capabilities but weak single-core performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores fall into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively, with single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also registering as poor. However, multi-threaded workloads perform significantly better, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression all achieving average tier results. Memory bandwidth remains consistently in the average range for both small and large block read/write operations, though the PassMark memory score is weak.

Given its massive memory capacity relative to compute resources, the M32ms is designed for memory-intensive workloads rather than raw compute-bound tasks. It demonstrates average performance in database operations and Redis SET operations, making it suitable for large in-memory databases, caching layers, and enterprise applications requiring substantial RAM. The qualitative cost efficiency of this instance is centered on its high resource density for memory-bound applications, where the cost of provisioning massive RAM arrays is offset by the dedicated, stable memory allocation, despite the lower single-threaded CPU efficiency.
